title: Act II, Scene II

teacherSummary.text: Claudius and Gertrude have summoned Rosencrantz and Guildenstern to discover Hamlet's trouble. Ambassadors report Norway's peace. Polonius reads Hamlet's love letter and plans to spy. Hamlet mocks Polonius, sees through his friends, and welcomes travelling players. After the First Player weeps for Hecuba, Hamlet berates himself and plans a play to catch Claudius's conscience.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Though this be madness, yet there is method in’t” slowly and put it in my own words: After talking with Hamlet, Polonius says aside that though this is madness, there is method in it. Next, craft. I notice the aside, which lets Polonius speak truth he will not act on. The strongest word is “method”: it suggests Hamlet's madness has a pattern and purpose. Then, effect. What does Polonius notice about Hamlet's madness? My answer: Polonius half-sees that Hamlet's "madness" is controlled and pointed, but he still blames love; the line invites the audience to question whether Hamlet is mad or acting.
